text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- KANDIR: "WITHOUT RE-ELECTION, COUNTRY WILL GROW LESS"

Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said that, without presidential re-election and constitutional reforms, Brazil's economy will grow more slowly, risking "strong social tensions" and threatening the Real stabilization plan.
-- GREATER CONTROL SOUGHT OVER TRANSFER PRICES

Changes being considered by the Federal Revenue Service in Brazil's Income Tax on companies next year would affect mostly large multinationals. One proposal is to tighten control over transfer prices by which some firms escape tax payments.
-- SMALL BROKERAGES LOSE REVENUES
Greater competiton and lower trading volume on local stock markets has hurt Brazil's small brokerages. In the last two years, 10 brokerages have ceased to operate in the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange.
O GLOBO
-- KANDIR SEES ANNUAL GROWTH UP TO 9 PCT WITH RE-ELECTION

Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said yesterday that the Brazilian economy will grow between seven and nine percent annually if Congress approves a constitutional amendment to allow presidential re-election.
-- BEACHES BECOME SCENE FOR SECOND ELECTION ROUND

In search of a place in the second-round run-off vote for Rio de Janeiro mayor, mayoral candidates Sergio Cabral Filho of the Social Democratic party and Chico Alencar of the Workers Party stumped along the city's southern beaches.
-- NETANYAHU AND ARAFAT TO DISCUSS PEACE IN THE U.S.
Israeli premier Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, invited by U.S. President Bill Cinton, will take part in peace talks set for Tuesday in Washington.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- THIRTY PERCENT OF VOTERS DON'T KNOW CANDIDATES' NUMBERS
Three days from mayoral elections, some 30 percent of voters do not know the ballot numbers of the candidate in Sao Paulo's mayoral race, a poll by the newspaper said.
-- PALMEIRAS BEATS SAO PAULO 2-1 AND LEADS IN CHAMPIONSHIP
Palmeiras soccer team retook the lead in the Brazilian soccer championship by defeating chief rival Sao Paulo football club 2-1.
-- BANKS FEAR GOV'T WILL LOSE GROUND WITH RE-ELECTION
Foreign creditor banks fear President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's campaign for a change in the constitution to allow him to run for re-election will bring problems with Congress.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
